title: Wi-Fi and network access: can anyone with a password get onto your network?
short: Move staff Wi-Fi to device certificates (EAP-TLS) within 6 months; since October 2026 Windows blocks saved MS-CHAPv2 sign-ins.
answer: Move staff Wi-Fi to EAP-TLS with a certificate on every managed device within six months, and give guests and devices that can't do 802.1X their own SSIDs and VLANs now. Judge every other measure by whether a stolen password, a copied MAC address or a laptop plugged into a meeting-room port still reaches more than the internet.
audience: IT and network teams running office, warehouse and plant networks, especially with Microsoft Intune and Entra ID

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Give every device its own certificate.
items.text: Use EAP-TLS with device certificates from Intune, issued by Microsoft Cloud PKI or your own CA. The NCSC calls this the most effective way to control which devices join[^ncscshadow].

items.title: Retire PEAP-MSCHAPv2.
items.text: A fake access point can capture the exchange and recover the password[^msadv]. Windows stopped using it automatically under Credential Guard[^credguard] and, in October 2026, by default[^ntlmv1].

items.title: Make every client check the RADIUS server.
items.text: Set the trusted root and server names in each Wi-Fi profile, so users never get asked to trust a certificate[^intunewifi]. Under WPA3-Enterprise, Windows 11 stops if validation fails[^eapwin11].

items.title: Segment guests and devices without 802.1X.
items.text: Put guest Wi-Fi in its own VLAN with internet only: in 2026, researchers broke client isolation on every network they tested[^airsnitch]. Limit devices known only by MAC address to what they need[^bsinac].

items.title: Lock down wired ports in public areas.
items.text: Run 802.1X with MAC fallback on ports in meeting rooms and reception, and switch off unused ones. In multi-host mode, one authorized client opens the port for all[^ciscohost], so a hub lets others in[^ncscshadow].

items.title: List what connects where.
items.text: For each SSID and switch, note the device types and whether they support 802.1X. BSI bases NAC planning on a complete asset inventory[^bsinac].

items.title: Choose the RADIUS server.
items.text: NPS accepts only certificates from an enterprise CA or mapped to an AD account[^npscert] and lacks TLS 1.3[^eapwin11], which hides device identities[^rfc9190]. For devices joined only to Entra ID, use a cloud RADIUS service that trusts your Intune CA.

items.title: Issue device certificates.
items.text: Deploy a trusted root profile and a SCEP profile, with key storage set to **Enroll to Trusted Platform Module (TPM) KSP, otherwise fail**[^scep]. Cloud PKI needs a license on top of Intune Plan 1 or 2[^cloudpki]; the encryption sheet covers private CAs.

items.title: Deploy the Wi-Fi profile.
items.text: Choose EAP-TLS, the SCEP certificate and **Machine** authentication[^intunewifi]; the mobile devices sheet covers phones. Turn on WPA3 where APs and clients support it: 6 GHz requires it[^wfa], as does enterprise Wi-Fi 7 on Windows 11[^wifi7].

items.title: Run both, then remove the old network.
items.text: Move groups over while watching RADIUS logs. Then delete the PSK or PEAP network and its profiles.

blocks.title: Run the RADIUS server as infrastructure
items: **Place it in the management zone.** Accept requests only from access points, controllers and switches, and alert when RADIUS is down or request counts jump[^bsinac].

**Harden RADIUS over UDP.** CVE-2024-3596 lets an attacker on the RADIUS network forge packets. On NPS, require Message-Authenticator and turn on `requireMsgAuth`; both are off by default[^blastradius].
**Plan for RADIUS being down.** Keep existing sessions and reject new ones, or assign a fixed restricted VLAN. Depending on the switch, an outage can otherwise open ports completely[^bsinac].

blocks.title: Printers, cameras, scanners and IoT
items: **Use certificates where the device can.** Intune SCEP profiles support Wi-Fi on Android Enterprise dedicated devices, such as scanners[^scep].

**Otherwise give each device its own key.** BSI allows shared identities only as justified exceptions[^bsinac]. Meraki's identity PSK, for example, gives each key its own policy, though not with WPA3[^ipsk]. Use 20 or more characters[^bsiwlan].
**Treat MAC authentication as a label.** It makes spoofing easy, so BSI wants such devices restricted to the minimum and profiled[^bsinac].
**One SSID or VLAN per device class,** reaching only its server; see the network segmentation sheet.

blocks.title: Rogue access points and evil twins
items: **Use your access points as sensors.** NIST recommends continuous monitoring for rogue APs, unauthorized clients and impersonation[^nist153].
**Scan where sensors don't reach** at least quarterly, NIST suggests, and assess the whole WLAN yearly[^nist153].
**Ban private access points.** BSI requires the ban in the usage policy[^bsiuse].
**Block bridging on laptops,** as NIST advises[^nist153]. APT28 used hacked dual-homed computers nearby to join a target's Wi-Fi that asked for no MFA[^volexity].

blocks.title: Controllers and cloud dashboards
items: **Sign in through your identity provider,** with phishing-resistant MFA, and keep one emergency local account. The edge devices sheet covers management interfaces.
**Patch within the patching sheet's deadlines** and change the defaults: BSI requires new SSIDs, passwords and keys before use, and encrypted admin access only[^bsiwlan].
**Log every change** centrally[^bsinac]; alert on new SSIDs, keys and RADIUS servers.
**Mount access points out of reach.** A stolen AP can reveal the RADIUS secret or the network key[^bsiwlan].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Windows ended automatic MS-CHAPv2 sign-in.** Since 13 October 2026, Windows 11 24H2 and later block single sign-on with NTLMv1-derived credentials, so PEAP-MSCHAPv2 no longer connects on its own. Setting `BlockNtlmv1SSO` to 0 is a temporary exception[^ntlmv1].
**Cloud PKI came to Microsoft 365 E5** from July 2026. Otherwise it's an add-on at $2 per user per month, paid yearly[^intuneprice].
**Client isolation proved leaky.** In February 2026, researchers bypassed it under WPA2 and WPA3, in home and enterprise networks; a separate guest VLAN stopped the attacks[^airsnitch].
**Network access systems were exploited.** CISA listed UniFi OS flaws in June 2026 and a Cisco ISE flaw in September 2026 as exploited[^kev].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Hidden SSIDs.** Clients announce the name anyway, and Microsoft advises against hiding it[^nonbroadcast].
**MAC allow-lists as access control.** BSI doesn't treat devices identified by MAC address as trusted[^bsinac].
**A VPN over your own Wi-Fi.** BSI lists it only for high protection needs[^bsiwlan].
**NAC posture checks before the basics.** BSI files them under high protection[^bsinac]. Check compliance at app sign-in with Conditional Access.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Letting users accept unknown servers.** With PEAP, that hands a fake AP a crackable response[^msadv]. Turn on **Perform server validation**[^intunewifi].
**Deleting a leaver before retiring the device.** Intune SCEP and PKCS certificates stay valid; retire or wipe the device first[^intunerevoke].
**Leaving `BlockNtlmv1SSO` at 0.** It reduces protection[^ntlmv1]; set an end date.
**One network for staff, guests and devices.** BSI forbids WLANs that couple security zones[^bsiwlan].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Ask your IT provider for EAP-TLS with Cloud PKI and cloud RADIUS instead of a staff password.
Put guests on their own SSID and VLAN with internet only, and printers and cameras on another.
Switch off network ports in meeting rooms and reception that nobody uses.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Put all managed devices on EAP-TLS; allow PEAP-MSCHAPv2 only as a named exception with an end date.
Enable 802.1X with MAC fallback on access switches, public areas first.
Turn on rogue AP detection and send RADIUS and controller logs to the SIEM.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Run redundant RADIUS servers in the management zone, separate for office and production[^bsinac].
Consider MACsec on ports in public areas[^bsinac].
In Germany, map controls to BSI NET.2.1, NET.2.2 and NET.3.4.

changes.text: First draft, based on BSI IT-Grundschutz NET.2.1, NET.2.2 and NET.3.4, NIST SP 800-153, NCSC guidance, Microsoft Learn pages on Intune, Cloud PKI, NPS and Credential Guard, and Microsoft's October 2026 MS-CHAPv2 change.
